title: Tycho Brahe observes a new star in Cassiopeia
summary: The Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe noticed a bright new star in the constellation Cassiopeia and measured that it showed no parallax, so it lay far beyond the Moon.
reason: The star was a supernova, and Tycho's careful measurements tested the belief that the heavens never change.
significance: It undermined the Aristotelian idea of unchanging heavens and made Tycho's name in astronomy.
